skill.name: supabase-patterns
skill.description: Framework-generic Supabase guidance for secure RLS policies, migrations, typed clients, realtime subscriptions, and storage usage.
skill.summary: Apply reusable Supabase security and schema patterns across application projects.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, SQL examples, and Supabase client configuration examples. I found no prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or host reconnaissance intent. One semantic issue remains: the SECURITY DEFINER helper function examples need search_path and privilege hardening guidance.

remediation.issue: SECURITY DEFINER functions lack hardening guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add SET search_path, schema-qualified table references, and privilege notes to each SECURITY DEFINER example.

remediation.issue: Referenced realtime and storage cookbook files are missing.
remediation.suggestion: Add the referenced cookbooks or remove the execute instructions so users do not follow broken guidance.

remediation.issue: Remote-impacting CLI examples need stronger safety labels.
remediation.suggestion: Label db push and remote operations as user-approved commands and warn about production impact.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe SECURITY DEFINER Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The RLS cookbook defines helper functions with SECURITY DEFINER but does not set a fixed search_path or document privilege restrictions. This can create privilege escalation risk in PostgreSQL if copied directly.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited blocks directly show SECURITY DEFINER helper function examples without visible hardening in the same examples. The exact impact depends on deployment context, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Supabase projects fail when RLS, storage, and realtime rules are applied inconsistently. This skill gives reusable patterns for safer schemas, clients, and migrations.
actual_capabilities: Guides Supabase project setup with conventional folders and migration workflow.
Provides RLS policy patterns for ownership, team access, public reads, and soft deletes.
Shows typed client usage with generated TypeScript database types.
Documents realtime subscription setup and cleanup patterns.
Summarizes storage upload and public URL patterns.
Lists production checks for keys, RLS, storage, realtime, rate limiting, and CORS.
limitations: Only one cookbook file is present, so referenced realtime and storage cookbooks are unavailable.
Examples are generic and need project-specific table names, roles, and policies.
It does not validate migrations or run Supabase tests by itself.
It assumes users understand Supabase CLI setup and local credentials.

use_cases.title: Secure a New App
use_cases.description: Create tables with RLS policies before exposing Supabase data to client applications.

use_cases.title: Audit Existing Policies
use_cases.description: Review ownership, team, and public-read rules before a production release.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Guidance
use_cases.description: Use one reference for migrations, key handling, realtime scope, and storage policy reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Supabase Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the supabase-patterns skill to outline a secure Supabase setup for a new app with user-owned posts.

prompt_templates.title: Add RLS Policies
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the RLS cookbook to draft policies for posts where owners can write and public posts are readable.

prompt_templates.title: Review Realtime Exposure
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my planned realtime tables for sensitive data risks and propose safer subscriptions.

prompt_templates.title: Design Team Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Supabase RLS policies for teams with members, admins, soft deletes, and audit-ready migrations.

output_examples.input: Request to add owner-only RLS for posts.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends enabling RLS, adding SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE policies, and testing with user JWT claims.

output_examples.input: Request to review Supabase production readiness.
output_examples.output: The assistant returns a concise checklist covering RLS, key placement, storage policies, realtime scope, rate limiting, and CORS.
The assistant explains team membership checks, admin update rules, helper functions, and migration organization.

best_practices: Enable RLS immediately after creating every table.
Keep service role keys out of client-side code.
Test policies with anonymous, authenticated, owner, and admin contexts.
anti_patterns: Creating tables first and adding RLS later.
Using broad authenticated-user policies for sensitive data.
Publishing realtime changes for tables with private fields.

faq.question: Does this skill run Supabase commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides command examples and patterns for an AI assistant to apply with user approval.

faq.question: Can it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. It supports review but cannot prove policies cover every data path.

faq.question: Which Supabase areas does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers RLS, migrations, typed clients, realtime subscriptions, storage patterns, and production checks.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can I use it with any framework?
faq.answer: Yes. The source states it is framework-generic and not tied to one project.

faq.question: What should I customize first?
faq.answer: Start with table names, ownership columns, team roles, and policies for sensitive data.
